To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) women who are avid exercisers are no less likely to be weight preoccupied than non-exercising or occasional exercising women; 2) women who are weight preoccupied are more emotionally reactive; 3) women who are emotionally reactive have a greater tendency to be dissatisfied with their body shape; and 4) women who are dissatisfied with their shape tend to be more concerned with their physical appearance and to have a lower self-esteem.

emotional reactivity is a predictor of weight preoccupation for both exercisers and non-exercisers; BMI is related to weight preoccupations in non-exercisers but not in exercisers; subjective body shape is related to weight and shape preoccupations in exercisers but not in non-exercising females; body dissatisfaction is associated with poor emotional well-being for exercisers but not for non-exercisers.

the possible psychological and social factors that influence the development of a preoccupation with body weight and appearance, particularly among women.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exercise is a double-edged sword.
there is a relationship between exercise and weight preoccupation, but that this is not a simple one.
the relationship between weight preoccupation and regular exercise is a complex one, and that the relationship between exercise and weight preoccupation is probably not a causal one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exercise is not a cure for body-image problems.
exercise does not necessarily lead to an increase in weight preoccupation, but it may increase a woman's body image dissatisfaction and her concern for physical appearance.
exercise may be a factor in the development of eating disorders but it may also serve as a means of coping with eating problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the more you exercise, the more you care about your appearance.
women who are highly invested in their physical appearance may be more likely than others to engage in vigorous exercise.
exercise is not the answer to the problem of weight preoccupation.
